newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil adoption program gets Internet address.
newsitem.headline: Brazil adoption program gets Internet address.

text.p: Interested parents can now find Rio de Janeiro's new adoption service on the Internet computer network under the address http://www.tj.rj.gov.br/, a Rio de Janeiro court official said on Friday.
The programme, which offers 40 orphans from the city of Rio de Janeiro for adoption, was announced in July. It is available in four languages: Portuguese, English, French and Spanish.

The service lists the children with photographs and personal data such as age, sex, race or criminal records, to make selection easier for Brazilians or foreigners seeking to adopt a child. The same legal provisions as for regular adoptions still apply when adopting through the Internet.

The number of children listed on the Internet service will be increased to around 50 in the coming weeks and will be updated continuously, said a spokeswoman for Rio de Janeiro's court, which founded the service.
There are 4,800 orphans in the city of Rio alone and 50 to 60 adoption cases are handled by the courts every month.
